name: Gabon
headline: Gabon: +3.2% growth in 2025, 1.8% inflation, debt 84% of GDP
sections: Gabon is a $21.9 billion economy (2025), the world's 133rd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.2% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $22K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 19.1% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 1.8% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 4.3% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 20.2% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 36.3% (2025).
Gross government debt is 84% of GDP (2025), a elevated level. The general government balance is −12.1% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −6.0% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 85% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.8% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 124% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 68.5 years (2024). Population: 2.3 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
